newsitem.title: UK: LCE coffee ends sharply down on NY, sees support.
newsitem.headline: LCE coffee ends sharply down on NY, sees support.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures traced New York down as profit taking continued to weigh on both markets, but traders cited good trade support limiting losses.
"Generally it has done quite well. It just needs some back up from fundamentals to keep it going," said one trader.
The benchmark November contract closed $57 down on Wednesday at $1,633 a tonne, hovering just around the critical support area which technical analysts reckon should hold.
It opened $40 lower after sharp losses in New York on Tuesday and dived to a session low of $1,629. It then recovered slightly.
Volume on the Exchange totalled 4,234 lots.
Traders said cool weather in Brazil was providing background support, keeping the downside potential limited.
Technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge said this week's slide had hinted that the market could have seen the best of its strength for now.
Traders said New York's September contract could continue to be buoyed by supply concerns while only four delivery notices have been issued so far despite a large open interest level.
But they suspected the rally may not extend beyond the September delivery period when an abundant flow of coffee is expected.
New York remained pressured by speculative and commission house selling at midday but roaster buying trimmed losses.
